dossier.public_summary: The 1.6 Earth-radius dip looks planet-sized but only a few of the 6 transits match it and they alternate in depth, with strong odd-even difference and a second eclipse. The event is grazing, V-shaped and lasts too long for the star, pointing to a blended or grazing eclipsing binary rather than a planet.

reasons.why: 6 transits are not consistent; signal is dominated by a few deep outliers and sign-reversing shallow events, not a repeating planet transit.
reasons.value: p_consistent=6.022044194959138e-31, share_of_top_3=0.994, outliers 821 ppm (6.2 sigma), 692 ppm (5.1 sigma), 6 ppm (-5.7 sigma), -34 ppm (-5.1 sigma)

reasons.why: Strong odd/even difference and a real secondary eclipse near phase 0.615 with depth ~41% of the primary favor an eclipsing binary at twice the period, not a planet.
reasons.value: odd_even.diff_sigma=3.787 depth_odd_ppm=249.7 depth_even_ppm=458.8 depth_ratio=1.8; secondary.snr=9.445 phase=0.615 depth_ppm=145.9 depth_over_dip=0.4111

reasons.why: Very grazing, long V-shaped eclipse with stellar-density mismatch supports a grazing stellar companion, inconsistent with a central small-planet transit.

reasons.why: No neighbour can explain the dip (centroid inconclusive but no plausible neighbour), size/duration alone are planet-like, yet the binary indicators and xgboost low rank combine to make a grazing EB the best explanation.
